area: Minecraft 26.2 (Mojang mappings): client-side prediction of "would a charged respawn anchor explode here?" — DimensionType vs. the new net.minecraft.world.attribute.EnvironmentAttributes system, and whether the deciding data reaches the client.

signatures.notes: DOES NOT EXIST on 26.2. javap -p of DimensionType lists every member; there is no respawnAnchorWorks. Corroborated by a byte-level scan of all 10,952 .class files in minecraft-common.jar + minecraft-client-only.jar for the UTF8 constants 'respawnAnchorWorks', 'bedWorks', 'ultraWarm', 'piglinSafe' -> 0 hits for all four. All of those booleans collapsed into the EnvironmentAttributeMap.

Record component that replaced the old per-flag accessors. DimensionType is now `public final class ... extends java.lang.Record` with components (hasFixedTime, hasSkyLight, hasCeiling, hasEnderDragonFight, coordinateScale, minY, height, logicalHeight, infiniburn, ambientLight, monsterSettings, skybox, cardinalLightType, attributes, timelines, defaultClock). On a CLIENT this map is the syncable-filtered subset only — see NETWORK_CODEC below.

EnvironmentAttributes is an interface; id is minecraft:gameplay/respawn_anchor_works. Decompiled registration: register("gameplay/respawn_anchor_works", EnvironmentAttribute.builder(AttributeTypes.BOOLEAN).defaultValue(false)) — note NO .syncable() and NO .notPositional(). Builder defaults are isSyncable=false, isPositional=true. So: server-only data, and positional.

SERVER-ONLY (ServerLevel param) — not callable from client code. Full decompiled body is one line: `return (Boolean)level.environmentAttributes().getValue(EnvironmentAttributes.RESPAWN_ANCHOR_WORKS, pos);`. useWithoutItem() calls `if (!canSetSpawn(serverLevel, pos)) this.explode(state, serverLevel, pos);` and explode() is `private void explode(BlockState, ServerLevel, BlockPos)` — also server-only.
Also present: MIN_CHARGES, MAX_CHARGES (public static final int). canBeCharged() is private; the vanilla explode path requires state.getValue(CHARGE) != 0.

Covariant narrowing of LevelReader's `public abstract net.minecraft.world.attribute.EnvironmentAttributeReader environmentAttributes();`. javap -p on Level prints BOTH lines — the EnvironmentAttributeReader one is the synthetic bridge, not a second overload.

Client-visible. Backed by `private final EnvironmentAttributeSystem environmentAttributes;` built in the ctor: `this.environmentAttributes = this.addEnvironmentAttributeLayers(EnvironmentAttributeSystem.builder()).build();` where addEnvironmentAttributeLayers calls `environmentAttributes.addDefaultLayers(this)`. Ticked via `this.environmentAttributes().invalidateTickCache();`.
This is the overload RespawnAnchorBlock.canSetSpawn uses. Body: `return this.getValue(attribute, Vec3.atCenterOf(pos));` -> `getValue(attribute, pos, null)`.

DO NOT use for RESPAWN_ANCHOR_WORKS. EnvironmentAttributeSystem's impl opens with `if (SharedConstants.IS_RUNNING_IN_IDE && attribute.isPositional()) throw new IllegalStateException("Position must always be provided for positional attribute " + attribute);`. RESPAWN_ANCHOR_WORKS is positional, so this is a hard crash in any dev launcher that flips IS_RUNNING_IN_IDE.

The one abstract positional accessor. Pass null for the interpolator; the biome layer then falls back to biomeManager.getNoiseBiomeAtPosition(pos.x, pos.y, pos.z). Also on the interface: `public static final EnvironmentAttributeReader EMPTY;` (returns attribute.defaultValue() for everything).

Only public entry points are builder(), invalidateTickCache(), getDimensionValue(...), getValue(attr, Vec3, SpatialAttributeInterpolator). Layers are baked per attribute at construction from: dimensionType().attributes() (constant layer) + per-biome positional layers + timeline time-based layers + weather layers. No way to read the raw dimension entry through it — use dimensionType().attributes() for that.

Also `public boolean isPositional();`, `public boolean isSpatiallyInterpolated();`, `public Value defaultValue();`. Builder defaults (decompiled): isSyncable=false, isPositional=true, isSpatiallyInterpolated=false. RESPAWN_ANCHOR_WORKS therefore reports isSyncable()==false, isPositional()==true.

Decompiled: `NETWORK_CODEC = CODEC.xmap(EnvironmentAttributeMap::filterSyncable, EnvironmentAttributeMap::filterSyncable)` with `filterSyncable = Maps.filterKeys(entries, EnvironmentAttribute::isSyncable)`. xmap applies it on DECODE as well as encode, so a client that parses a dimension_type through this codec drops every non-syncable attribute. This is a read of the codec chain, not an executed round-trip — I did not stand up a JVM with the MC classpath to decode a JSON and print keySet().

Useful as the direct client-side probe of whether the attribute survived sync: level.dimensionType().attributes().contains(EnvironmentAttributes.RESPAWN_ANCHOR_WORKS) should be false on a client. Also public: `<Value> Entry<Value,?> get(EnvironmentAttribute<Value>)`, `<Value> Value applyModifier(EnvironmentAttribute<Value>, Value)`, `Set<EnvironmentAttribute<?>> keySet()`, `static Builder builder()`, `static final EnvironmentAttributeMap EMPTY`.

`NETWORK_CODEC = createDirectCodec(EnvironmentAttributeMap.NETWORK_CODEC)` vs `DIRECT_CODEC = createDirectCodec(EnvironmentAttributeMap.CODEC)`. Every other record field uses the identical codec in both — `attributes` is the ONLY field that differs between disk and wire.

= ByteBufCodecs.holderRegistry(Registries.DIMENSION_TYPE), which is `registry(key, Registry::asHolderIdMap)` — pure numeric-id, no direct-value fallback. Consequence: the Holder<DimensionType> a client gets is always a keyed Holder.Reference resolved out of its own synced DIMENSION_TYPE registry, so .is(ResourceKey) works on it.

Contains `new RegistryData(Registries.DIMENSION_TYPE, DimensionType.NETWORK_CODEC)` and `new RegistryData(Registries.BIOME, Biome.NETWORK_CODEC)`. The separate WORLDGEN_REGISTRIES list (server/disk) uses DimensionType.DIRECT_CODEC. Client path: ClientConfigurationPacketListenerImpl -> RegistryDataCollector.loadNewElementsAndTags -> RegistryDataLoader.load(entriesToLoad, knownDataSource, ..., RegistryDataLoader.SYNCHRONIZED_REGISTRIES, ...) -> ClientRegistryLayer.REMOTE.

signatures.member: PendingRegistration.loadFromNetwork(this.data.elementCodec(), nbtOps, elementKey, networkContents.get()) / PendingRegistration.findAndLoadFromResource(this.data.elementCodec(), jsonOps, elementKey, knownDataPathConverter, this.knownDataSource)
signatures.notes: Both branches use data.elementCodec() — i.e. NETWORK_CODEC. So the known-pack shortcut (client reads minecraft:the_nether from its OWN local jar data instead of the wire) is filtered exactly the same way. There is no path by which a client ends up with the unfiltered attribute map.

Biome.DIRECT_CODEC uses EnvironmentAttributeMap.CODEC_ONLY_POSITIONAL for "attributes"; Biome.NETWORK_CODEC uses EnvironmentAttributeMap.NETWORK_CODEC. RESPAWN_ANCHOR_WORKS is positional, so a datapack biome legally CAN override it — and that override is also stripped from the client. Second unsynced source of truth.

= ResourceKey.create(Registries.DIMENSION, Identifier.withDefaultNamespace("overworld")). Siblings NETHER = "the_nether", END = "the_end", same shape. Note the registry key is Registries.DIMENSION (not DIMENSION_TYPE).
minecraft:the_nether.
minecraft:the_end.

THE client-side test to use. Backed by `private final Holder<DimensionType> dimensionTypeRegistration;` set from the Level ctor's Holder<DimensionType> param. Sibling `public net.minecraft.world.level.dimension.DimensionType dimensionType();` returns the unwrapped record.

= ResourceKey.create(Registries.DIMENSION_TYPE, Identifier.withDefaultNamespace("the_nether")). Siblings OVERWORLD, END, OVERWORLD_CAVES. Verified against the shipped data: data/minecraft/dimension_type/the_nether.json is the ONLY vanilla dimension_type with "minecraft:gameplay/respawn_anchor_works": true; overworld.json and the_end.json both set it false; overworld_caves.json reuses the overworld attribute map.

Holder.Reference impl is `return this.key() == key;` (identity — safe because ResourceKey interns via a weak-valued ConcurrentMap and does NOT override equals). Holder.Direct impl is `return false;` unconditionally — harmless here since holderRegistry never emits a Direct holder.

Record component decoded with `DimensionType.STREAM_CODEC.decode(input)`; the sibling `ResourceKey<Level> dimension()` is decoded with `input.readResourceKey(Registries.DIMENSION)`. This is what feeds the ClientLevel ctor: `public ClientLevel(ClientPacketListener, ClientLevel$ClientLevelData, ResourceKey<Level>, Holder<DimensionType>, int, int, LevelExtractor, boolean, long, int)`.

`this.registryAccess = cookie.receivedRegistries();` — the REMOTE layer built by RegistryDataCollector, i.e. the network-filtered copy. ClientLevel's ctor passes exactly this into super(...): `super(levelData, dimension, connection.registryAccess(), dimensionType, true, isDebug, biomeZoomSeed, 1000000);`. Singleplayer is not special-cased — the integrated server goes through the same configuration handshake.

Registered WITH .syncable() and vanilla nether sets it true while overworld/end leave it at default false — so this one IS readable client-side and correlates with the nether. Same for FAST_LAVA (syncable, nether=true). Useful only as a heuristic for datapack nether-alikes; neither implies respawn_anchor_works.

26.2 relocation: BlockState no longer gets is(Block) from StateHolder/BlockStateBase. BlockBehaviour$BlockStateBase now `implements net.minecraft.core.TypedInstance<Block>`, which supplies is(T), is(Holder<T>), is(ResourceKey<T>), is(TagKey<T>), is(HolderSet<T>). So blockState.is(Blocks.RESPAWN_ANCHOR) still compiles, just from a different declaring type.
Public nullable field; `public static net.minecraft.client.Minecraft getInstance();`.
Where the interface-level accessor is declared, if you want a helper that takes LevelReader rather than ClientLevel.

gotchas: THE ONE THAT WILL BITE YOU: EnvironmentAttributes.RESPAWN_ANCHOR_WORKS is NOT syncable, so the obvious client-side mirror of canSetSpawn compiles, runs, throws nothing — and is wrong. Chain: RESPAWN_ANCHOR_WORKS is built without .syncable() (Builder default isSyncable=false) -> EnvironmentAttributeMap.NETWORK_CODEC = CODEC.xmap(filterSyncable, filterSyncable) where filterSyncable = Maps.filterKeys(entries, EnvironmentAttribute::isSyncable), and xmap filters on DECODE too -> DimensionType.NETWORK_CODEC = createDirectCodec(EnvironmentAttributeMap.NETWORK_CODEC) -> RegistryDataLoader.SYNCHRONIZED_REGISTRIES binds Registries.DIMENSION_TYPE to that NETWORK_CODEC -> the client's DimensionType.attributes() has no respawn_anchor_works entry -> EnvironmentAttributeSystem.getValue falls through to attribute.defaultValue(), which is false. Net effect: mc.level.environmentAttributes().getValue(EnvironmentAttributes.RESPAWN_ANCHOR_WORKS, pos) returns false in EVERY dimension on the client, including the vanilla Nether where the server answers true. A naive client check predicts 'anchor explodes' everywhere and gets the Nether exactly backwards.

DimensionType.respawnAnchorWorks() is gone, and so are bedWorks(), ultraWarm(), piglinSafe() and natural(). Verified by javap -p (full member list, none present) plus a byte-level scan of the UTF8 constant pools of all 10,952 classes across minecraft-common.jar and minecraft-client-only.jar: 0 hits for each of those four names. Those booleans are now EnvironmentAttributes entries inside DimensionType.attributes() (an EnvironmentAttributeMap record component).

Do NOT call getDimensionValue(EnvironmentAttributes.RESPAWN_ANCHOR_WORKS). EnvironmentAttributeSystem.getDimensionValue starts with `if (SharedConstants.IS_RUNNING_IN_IDE && attribute.isPositional()) throw new IllegalStateException("Position must always be provided for positional attribute " + attribute);` and RESPAWN_ANCHOR_WORKS is positional (Builder default isPositional=true; no .notPositional() call). SharedConstants.IS_RUNNING_IN_IDE is `public static boolean` with no initializer (false in the shipped jar) but is a mutable flag that dev launchers set — I did not verify whether Loom's runClient sets it, so treat the throw as live. Always use the positional overload getValue(attr, pos).

RespawnAnchorBlock.canSetSpawn takes ServerLevel, and the explode path (private void explode(BlockState, ServerLevel, BlockPos)) is server-only too. There is no client-visible vanilla helper — I searched every class in both jars for a 'respawnAnchorWorks' method name (0 hits) and for any reference to the RESPAWN_ANCHOR_WORKS field: exactly three classes touch it, all in minecraft-common (EnvironmentAttributes, which declares it; RespawnAnchorBlock, the server-only gate; and data/worldgen DimensionTypes, the datagen bootstrap). Zero client classes read it. You must reimplement the predicate yourself.

The dimension type is only HALF the story even on the server. canSetSpawn goes through EnvironmentAttributeSystem, whose layers are dimensionType().attributes() (constant) PLUS a per-biome positional layer built from Biome.getAttributes(). RESPAWN_ANCHOR_WORKS is positional and Biome.DIRECT_CODEC accepts positional attributes (EnvironmentAttributeMap.CODEC_ONLY_POSITIONAL), so a datapack biome can flip it per-position. Biome.NETWORK_CODEC filters by isSyncable identically, so biome overrides are invisible to the client as well. No vanilla biome touches it.

Level.dimension() == Level.NETHER is NOT the same predicate as the dimension type. Level.NETWORK/OVERWORLD/END are ResourceKey<Level> in Registries.DIMENSION (the world id: minecraft:overworld / the_nether / the_end); what canSetSpawn actually reads hangs off the DimensionType in Registries.DIMENSION_TYPE. A datapack can point a dimension named anything at the minecraft:the_nether dimension type (respawn anchors then work there), or give minecraft:the_nether a custom type. Prefer level.dimensionTypeRegistration().is(BuiltinDimensionTypes.NETHER) over a Level-key compare. It is safe: DimensionType.STREAM_CODEC is ByteBufCodecs.holderRegistry (id-only, no direct-value fallback), so the client's holder is always a keyed Holder.Reference and Holder.Reference.is(key) is `this.key() == key`; Holder.Direct.is(ResourceKey) would return false unconditionally but never occurs on this path.

Everything ELSE on DimensionType is synced faithfully — DIRECT_CODEC and NETWORK_CODEC are the same createDirectCodec() call and differ only in the codec handed to the "attributes" field. So hasCeiling(), coordinateScale(), skybox(), cardinalLightType(), ambientLight(), minY()/height()/logicalHeight(), monsterSettings(), infiniburn(), timelines(), defaultClock() are all trustworthy client-side. Two syncable attributes also correlate with the vanilla Nether and ARE readable client-side: WATER_EVAPORATES and FAST_LAVA (both .syncable(), both true only in the_nether.json). They are heuristics, not the real gate.

javap -p on Level prints TWO environmentAttributes() lines — `public abstract ...EnvironmentAttributeSystem environmentAttributes()` and `public ...EnvironmentAttributeReader environmentAttributes()`. The second is the synthetic covariant bridge for LevelReader.environmentAttributes(); it is not an overload and there is nothing to disambiguate. Same story for ClientLevel (which prints both EnvironmentAttributeSystem and EnvironmentAttributeReader) and for clockManager().

Unrelated 26.2 renames you will hit writing this code: ResourceLocation is now net.minecraft.resources.Identifier (ResourceKey.create(..., Identifier.withDefaultNamespace("the_nether"))), and BlockState.is(Block) now comes from the new net.minecraft.core.TypedInstance<Block> interface rather than StateHolder/BlockBehaviour$BlockStateBase — grep BlockStateBase for `boolean is(` and you will only find is(TagKey, Predicate) and be misled.

Epistemic note on the sync claim: it is established by reading the full decompiled codec/loader chain (EnvironmentAttribute.Builder defaults -> EnvironmentAttributeMap.NETWORK_CODEC -> DimensionType.NETWORK_CODEC -> RegistryDataLoader.SYNCHRONIZED_REGISTRIES -> NetworkRegistryLoadTask (both the network AND known-pack-local-resource branches use data.elementCodec()) -> RegistryDataCollector -> ClientPacketListener.registryAccess() -> ClientLevel ctor -> EnvironmentAttributeSystem.addDimensionLayer), corroborated by the shipped data/minecraft/dimension_type/the_nether.json actually containing "minecraft:gameplay/respawn_anchor_works": true. I did not stand up a JVM with the Minecraft classpath to decode that JSON through NETWORK_CODEC and print the surviving keySet(); if you want a runtime assertion, level.dimensionType().attributes().contains(EnvironmentAttributes.RESPAWN_ANCHOR_WORKS) should be false on any client and true on a server.
